skill.name: resource-monitor

content.value_statement: Resource problems can slow applications and hide capacity risks. This skill guides CPU, memory, disk, network, and process monitoring with clear reports.
actual_capabilities: Lists common commands for CPU, memory, disk, network, and process checks.
Provides Node.js and Python examples for periodic resource logging.
Shows alert thresholds for CPU, memory, disk, and network conditions.
Includes a structured monitoring report template with metrics and recommendations.
Supports capacity planning through trend and threshold analysis.
References common monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, and CloudWatch.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a packaged monitoring agent.
Some commands require Linux utilities that may not exist on every host.
It does not store historical metrics unless users add external storage.
Network and process visibility depends on local permissions and operating system settings.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Local Performance Issues
use_cases.description: Check CPU, memory, disk, and network activity while an application runs in development.

use_cases.title: Create Operations Health Reports
use_cases.description: Summarize daily resource usage, peaks, warnings, and recommended actions for a service.

use_cases.title: Plan Capacity Changes
use_cases.description: Review trends and thresholds to decide when storage, memory, or compute capacity should increase.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Resource Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check of the current machine.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use resource-monitor to help me check current CPU, memory, disk, and network usage. Explain the results in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Bottleneck
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate troubleshooting for a slow service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use resource-monitor to identify likely resource bottlenecks for my service. Focus on high CPU, memory pressure, disk space, and network saturation.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Alert Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use resource-monitor to propose warning and critical thresholds for CPU, memory, disk, and network usage for a production web service.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Capacity Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use resource-monitor to turn these resource observations into an operations report with risks, trends, recommended actions, and capacity planning notes.

output_examples.input: Review a server that peaks at 87 percent CPU and 85 percent memory during report generation.
output_examples.output: The report highlights a short CPU and memory peak, links it to scheduled reporting, and recommends moving heavy work off peak.

output_examples.input: Summarize disk usage when logs grow by 1.2 GB each day.
output_examples.output: The summary flags log growth as the main storage risk and recommends rotation, archiving, and weekly trend checks.

output_examples.input: Assess whether current network capacity is enough for the next quarter.
output_examples.output: The assessment compares average and peak bandwidth, notes current headroom, and recommends alerting on connection errors.

best_practices: Establish normal baselines before tuning thresholds or alerts.
Correlate resource spikes with deployments, jobs, and traffic changes.
Keep monitoring reports short, dated, and tied to clear recommended actions.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad diagnostics on systems you are not authorized to inspect.
Do not treat one short spike as a trend without historical context.
Do not create noisy alerts for conditions that require no action.

faq.question: Does this skill install a monitoring agent?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands, examples, thresholds, and report structure for monitoring workflows.

faq.question: Can it monitor CPU and memory usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands and script examples for CPU, load average, memory, and process memory checks.

faq.question: Does it support disk and network checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers disk space, disk I/O, directory growth, network traffic, and connection summaries.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production operations?
faq.answer: It can support production reviews, but users should validate commands, permissions, and thresholds for their environment.

faq.question: Does it replace Prometheus or Grafana?
faq.answer: No. It can help plan and interpret monitoring, but dedicated tools should collect and store long-term metrics.
